about: American Chopper Argument is a six-panel grid of Paul Teutul Jr. and his father, Paul Teutul Sr., from the reality show American Chopper, screaming at each other in a cluttered office. Jr. in a black cap jabs his finger and yells; Sr., with his gray walrus mustache and tattooed arms, yells back from his desk; the shouting escalates until a chair goes flying and Sr. is left pointing and roaring. Because each panel is a turn in the argument, the format is used to stage a heated back-and-forth over something, often a nerdy or trivial debate presented with absurd intensity.
origin: The fight aired on Discovery Channel's American Chopper in 2009 and is about Jr. showing up late to work. The six-shot meme format took off in 2018.
usage:
Each of the six boxes is one line of dialogue, alternating between the two men in reading order: left panel, right panel, row by row. The argument should escalate, with each line rebutting the last, and the final box landing a twist or contradiction.

The joke is fury over nuance. Debates about technical definitions, grammar, fandom lore or obscure rules work best when both sides make real points. Write it as a genuine argument; the image supplies the shouting.
